content: S3 one status (waits on S2): liveness becomes the holder's own session status plus one predicate for a holder that can never return; delete SwarmMemberRuntime.todo_items (the third copy of a session's rows), the four member shapes and the third event log. Gate: the member cache gone, one predicate decides liveness, the TUI reads the typed status.

S5 status, priority and group leave TaskItem, with the status vocabularies they keep alive: the status helpers in kcode-plan/src/lib.rs and canonical_todo_status plus its two wrappers in kcode-base/src/todo.rs. S2 took the TUI's (t31 took newly_ready_item_ids), so the field drop is what remains. Afterwards readiness is blocked_by empty and liveness comes from the member, not the item. Gate: the three fields gone and the vocabularies with them.

D2 the swarm/comm condense: the SwarmState handle pair is rebuilt as a literal at each request arm and threaded to ~40 functions; give the swarm state its one owner and delete the pair. This is the work that gates plans/server-shape.md H2. Gate: no SwarmState literal at a request arm.
G1 restore the two size ratchets in scripts/check_guardrails.sh and re-baseline both with --update; they are paused with the reason at the call site.

G2 the one live kcode run probe against its own socket, in a scratch repo, run by the user: the permission (a granted turn continues, a wake does not) and the poke's removal (no client continuation; every non-retryable error gets the short budget). It is the lane's landing proof, so it runs when the list is done, not per step.

note: S4 (t17), G3 (t24) and S2 (t15, four children t26-t29, -6,384 lines) landed 2026-10-04, then S2's deadwood (t31, -5,116 lines). S3 (t16) is now the next step; S5 (t18) waits on it. Also open: t32 (the roster's output tap and the inline spawn mode), t30 (the live TUI check), t20 (D2), t22 (G1), t23 (the socket probe, the user's), t25.

content: The live TUI smoke test for S2 and S3, deferred so it exercises both at once: build a fresh kcode, in a scratch repo add rows with the todo tool (two roots, one child naming a root as parent, one row blocked by another), confirm the pinned list shows id + words, the child indented, the blocked row marked and no card/page/pips/roster surface; run /auto (or spawn a worker) so a member takes a row and its glyph animates with @name, model and age; stop the holder mid-row and the row goes red; close a blocker and the mark clears. Steps in docs/plans/task-flow.md under S3. Gate: each observed screen matches, step by step.

The roster's output tap goes, with the spawn mode that was its only switch. set_inline_output_tap (enabled only for SwarmSpawnMode::Inline) publishes BusEvent::SwarmOutputTail from the streaming path, background_tasks stores it as member.output_tail, and the status broadcast ships SwarmMemberStatus.output_tail to a client that never reads it. Delete the tap flag, the bus event and its dispatcher, the member field and the wire field; then Inline behaves exactly like Headless, so collapse the variant (keep "inline" as a parse alias so existing configs keep working, re-default to Headless) or say the name is worth keeping. Fix the docs that still claim a gallery viewport: the Inline variant comment, default_file.rs, config_file.rs. Gate: no reader of output_tail or the tap outside tests; check --workspace --all-targets and clippy -D warnings clean.

S2's other deadwood: the swarm output tap. The gallery viewport was the only reader of a member's output tail, so delete the chain that feeds it: Agent::set_inline_output_tap with inline_output_tap and the tap branches in turn_streaming_mpsc (6 sites) plus turn_execution's BusEvent::SwarmOutputTail publish; kcode-base/src/bus.rs's SwarmOutputTail type and bus variant; server.rs's dispatch arm; background_tasks::dispatch_swarm_output_tail; SwarmMemberRuntime.output_tail (server/state.rs) with its write at background_tasks.rs:239 and clear at swarm.rs:978; SwarmMemberStatus.output_tail on the wire; headless.rs's tap enable for the inline spawn mode; and the TUI debug fixture that injects sample tails. Keep the unrelated background-task output tail (kcode-background-types, kcode-base/src/background.rs, message previews): same name, different concept. With the tap gone, SwarmSpawnMode::Inline behaves exactly like Headless (comm_session already groups them), so collapse the variant into Headless and keep "inline" as a parse alias so existing configs still load, or re-document it. Gate: no producer or reader of a swarm output tail left; cargo check --workspace --all-targets and clippy -D warnings clean.
